title: EARLY Act Reauthorization of 2025

claims.claim: The underlying Act is the Young Women's Breast Health Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act of 2009.
claims.sourceSpan: Requires Learning Young Act of 2009

claims.claim: It is Section 399NN of the Public Health Service Act, 42 U.S.C. 280m.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 399NN(h) of the Public Health Service Act
claims.note: Section 399NN / 42 U.S.C. 280m confirmed in bill text and in the referencedSource heading.

claims.claim: The Act directs CDC to run a national evidence-based public education campaign.
claims.sourceSpan: shall conduct a national evidence-based education campaign to increase awareness
claims.note: CDC = 'The Secretary, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention'.

claims.claim: The Act directs a health-care-professional education campaign.
claims.sourceSpan: Health care professional education campaign

claims.claim: The campaigns cover breast health, symptoms, early detection, and support for young women diagnosed with breast cancer.
claims.sourceSpan: breast health, symptoms, and early diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer in young women
claims.note: Early detection: (a)(1)(D); support: subsection (d).

claims.claim: 'Young women' are defined as women 15 to 44.
claims.sourceSpan: means women 15 to 44 years of age

claims.claim: The Act also funds prevention research.
claims.sourceSpan: conduct prevention research on breast cancer in younger women
claims.note: The (h) authorization funds (c)(1) CDC research; (c)(2) NIH research is not within (h).

claims.claim: The Act funds grants to organizations serving young women with breast cancer.
claims.sourceSpan: shall award grants to organizations and institutions to provide health information from credible sources and substantive assistance directed to young women diagnosed with breast cancer

claims.claim: This bill extends the authorization by striking '2026' in subsection (h) and inserting '2031'.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''

claims.claim: It extends the $9M-per-year authorization through fiscal year 2031.
claims.sourceSpan: $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026
claims.note: $9M = $9,000,000; through-FY2031 derived from striking 2026 / inserting 2031.

claims.claim: The EARLY Act young women's breast health and support program is CDC-run.
claims.sourceSpan: shall conduct a national evidence-based education campaign to increase awareness
claims.note: Program run by the Secretary acting through the CDC Director.

claims.claim: The bill extends the program's $9M-per-year authorization through fiscal year 2031.
claims.sourceSpan: $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026

claims.claim: CDC national public education campaign on breast health and early detection.
claims.sourceSpan: shall conduct a national evidence-based education campaign to increase awareness
claims.note: Early detection: (a)(1)(D).

claims.claim: Health-care-professional education campaign on symptoms, family history, referrals.
claims.sourceSpan: including specific risk factors such as family history of cancer
claims.note: Symptoms: (b)(1); referrals: (b)(4) and (b)(6).

claims.claim: Prevention research on breast cancer in younger women.
claims.sourceSpan: conduct prevention research on breast cancer in younger women

claims.claim: Grants to organizations providing information and support to young women diagnosed with breast cancer.
claims.sourceSpan: shall award grants to organizations and institutions to provide health information from credible sources and substantive assistance directed to young women diagnosed with breast cancer

claims.claim: 'Young women' defined as women 15 to 44 years of age.
claims.sourceSpan: means women 15 to 44 years of age

claims.claim: Strikes '2026' in Section 399NN(h) and inserts '2031'.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''

claims.claim: Extends the $9M-per-year authorization from FY2022-2026 through FY2031.
claims.sourceSpan: $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026
claims.note: FY2022-2026 verbatim; extension to FY2031 from the strike/insert.

claims.claim: No changes to the underlying program activities or eligibility.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''
claims.note: The bill's sole operative provision is the year strike/insert; no other amendments present.

claims.claim: Extends the EARLY Act authorization by striking '2026' and inserting '2031' in Section 399NN(h) (42 U.S.C. 280m(h)).
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''

claims.claim: The statute currently authorizes $9M for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026.
claims.sourceSpan: $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026

claims.claim: The authorization carries out subsections (a), (b), (c)(1), and (d).
claims.sourceSpan: To carry out subsections (a), (b), (c)(1), and (d)
claims.note: Subsection list verbatim in (h).

claims.claim: Subsection (a) is the public education campaign.
claims.sourceSpan: Public education campaign

claims.claim: Subsection (b) is health-care-professional education.
claims.sourceSpan: Health care professional education campaign

claims.claim: Subsection (c)(1) is CDC prevention research.
claims.sourceSpan: the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, shall conduct prevention research on breast cancer in younger women
claims.note: Correctly scopes to (c)(1) CDC; (c)(2) NIH research is excluded from the (h) authorization.

claims.claim: Subsection (d) is support for young women diagnosed with breast cancer.
claims.sourceSpan: Support for young women diagnosed with breast cancer

claims.claim: The bill's one operative amendment shifts the end year from 2026 to 2031 without changing the dollar figure or the scope of covered activities.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''
claims.note: Only the year is amended; no dollar or scope change in the bill text.

claims.claim: Section 399NN(h) (42 U.S.C. 280m(h)) authorization end year shifted from '2026' to '2031', extending the $9M-per-year authorization through FY2031.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''

claims.claim: The bill adds and removes nothing (only modifies).
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''
claims.note: Sole provision is an amendment; added[]/removed[] correctly empty.

claims.claim: The bill extends through FY2031 but does not adjust the $9M-per-year dollar figure.
claims.sourceSpan: $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026
claims.note: Bill changes only the year.

claims.claim: The $9M amount has been held flat since the 2020 amendment (Public Law 116-260).
claims.sourceSpan: Pub. L. 116–260 substituted
claims.note: Editorial note: 2020 Pub. L. 116-260 substituted '$9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026'.

claims.claim: The $9M amount is not indexed for inflation.
claims.sourceSpan: $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026
claims.note: Flat-dollar figure with no indexing language in the statute — absence supportable.

claims.claim: The bill continues the 'young women' statutory definition of women 15 to 44.
claims.sourceSpan: means women 15 to 44 years of age

claims.claim: The underlying statute flags Ashkenazi Jewish populations as a higher-risk group.
claims.sourceSpan: such as Ashkenazi Jewish populations

claims.claim: The underlying statute flags racial and ethnic minority groups as higher-risk populations.
claims.sourceSpan: breast health in young women of all racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds
claims.note: Source frames as 'all racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds' and risk in 'high-risk populations'; 'minority groups' is an editorial gloss, not verbatim — non-material.

claims.claim: The bill does not modify the Advisory Committee established under Section 399NN(a)(4), including its membership.
claims.sourceSpan: shall establish an advisory committee to assist in creating and conducting the education campaigns
claims.note: Advisory committee (Establishment) and Membership are under (a)(4); the bill makes no change.

claims.claim: The Advisory Committee (Section 399NN(a)(4)) has reporting obligations to Congress.
claims.sourceSpan: submit reports to the Congress on the results of such measurements
claims.section: 42 U.S.C. 280m(f) Measurement; reporting — the Secretary via CDC, NOT the Advisory Committee (a)(4)
claims.note: Right fact, wrong account: reporting to Congress is imposed on the Secretary (acting through the CDC Director) under subsection (f)(3). The Advisory Committee under (a)(4) has only Establishment and Membership provisions and no reporting-to-Congress duty. The gap's parallel construction ('its membership or its reporting obligations to Congress') wrongly binds the reporting duty to the Advisory Committee.

claims.claim: The bill continues the every-3-year impact measurement requirement under Section 399NN(f).
claims.sourceSpan: not less than every 3 years, measure the impact of such activities
claims.note: Source: 'not less than every 3 years' (at least this often); 'every-3-year' is a fair paraphrase.

claims.claim: The bill does not require CDC to make its measurement data publicly available.
claims.sourceSpan: submit reports to the Congress on the results of such measurements
claims.note: Statute requires reports to Congress only; no public-availability mandate — absence supportable.

claims.claim: Introduced by Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz.
claims.sourceSpan: Ms. Wasserman Schultz

claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Fitzpatrick, Mrs. Dingell, and Mrs. Harshbarger
claims.note: All five named as original cosponsors in bill text (Miller-Meeks, Castor of Florida, Fitzpatrick, Dingell, Harshbarger); party labels are structural metadata. Cross-party is a factual structural observation, not breadth-of-support puffery.

claims.claim: The measure was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
claims.sourceSpan: Energy and Commerce

claims.note: Matches votes[] (Passed House 394-6, 2026-07-20) and stage 'Received in Senate' 2026-07-27; structural metadata, not in the introduced bill text.

claims.claim: Short reauthorizations of expiring CDC public-health authorizations that shift the year window without changing dollars typically clear the Senate by unanimous consent or voice.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended by striking ``2026'' and inserting ``2031''
claims.note: The 'shifts the year window without changing dollars' description of THIS bill is source-backed; the generalized Senate-passage prediction is analytical likelihood reasoning, not a source claim — acceptable in likelihoodReason, non-material.

claims.claim: Statute subsections (c)(2) NIH research and (e) no-duplication are not mentioned in the analysis.
claims.sourceSpan: the Director of the National Institutes of Health, shall conduct research
claims.note: Immaterial to a year-extension bill: (c)(2) NIH research is excluded from the (h) authorization and (e) is a housekeeping clause; the omission is reasonable, recorded for completeness.
